d: The Shintaphu glacial lake outburst flood occurs in the upper reaches of Bhutan, releasing about 7.4 million cubic metres of water. Bhutan evacuated people along the Mo Chhu river and further downstream, as the floodwaters destroyed highways and swept away the Gasa Tshachu hot spring complex. Firstpost looks at what caused the glacial flood, and what areas of Bhutan were impacted. Hem Kaur Saroya explains how the glacial flood endangered India, and how the states of West Bengal and Assam braced for the impact.
